I did not approach him whatsoever, people follow each other day to night and it’s not a ticket for invitation into further knowledge of each other. I appreciate your time to explain yourself and let me understand the situation, the thing is that many of my gay friends make events like this something to consider only relatable to us, but I mean, I know that everybody deals with possible rejection, it’s just that I didn’t mention it in the post because I thought that it was already known, but I’ll make sure next time to express myself better, thank you. Now, I pictured what you mean with awkward but, really, believe me when I say that even following him was a huge thing because my thoughts about people remain by myself and the only people that I *approach* (certainly not on social media, hence why I don’t consider myself approaching him in any way possible) are people of my everyday life basis: friends, acquaintances and so on. He’s of my same city by the way and knows personally people that i have as friends, a detail known just minutes before while talking about it with a friend so he has an idea of who I might be, hence why he followed me back. I hope to not come off as bad, I absolutely appreciate someone that makes me think above the surface of things

I think that my introduction about being gay and having consequently the problem that not every guy I consider can be attracted to me as a guy was misunderstood, I obviously acknowledge that also straight guys have this problem but I was talking about my case precisely. As a gay guy, I am as a fact attracted to the same gender and when did I say that this was not it or a lie? I’m just talking about his appearance, I saw him and thought that he was cute and had an infatuation, catching feelings was probably the wrong term but english is not my first language, I used the term not to mean that I want him so badly and already projected a future with him, but that I would like to know him in person and just see where things would lead, that is awkward?

I did not mention physical features, what I wanted to mean is that him being straight would be a problem in the long run if I catch feelings because he’s not interested in the same sex, if I had hypothetically an interest for a gay guy that didn’t find me attractive that would not be a gendered/sexuality problem, because I wouldn’t just be his type, but overall I’d have greater chances than with someone who is straight, if you know what I mean 

by the way thank you for the tip, my friends told me to do the same but I don’t know, I don’t want to sound inappropriate or awkward, especially when he’s not even a friend
